item.title: Fed's Barr flags AI risks to financial stability, warns of market disruption
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr warned that artificial intelligence could threaten financial stability through cyberattacks, automated trading and market manipulation. A Fed survey found 87% of respondents viewed AI as a significant financial risk, highlighting concerns over volatility, consumer protection, banking vulnerabilities and potential systemic disruptions.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Nagar
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr has warned that artificial intelligence could pose growing risks to financial markets, cybersecurity and consumer protection, raising concerns about the technology's potential to destabilise the financial system, according to a report by Reuters.Barr's remarks follow the US Federal Reserve's latest Financial Stability Report, released on Friday, which showed that 87% of surveyed contacts identified AI as a significant risk to the financial system. Concerns included AI-powered cyberattacks, complex financing arrangements and the possibility of a slowdown in AI-related earnings triggering a broader stock market decline.Also Read |South Korean stocks fall for fourth day as AI worries hit chipmakersAccording to Reuters, Barr on Monday highlighted additional risks, including the possibility that widespread reliance on AI-driven trading models could encourage herd behaviour and amplify market volatility. He also warned that self-learning algorithms could potentially manipulate markets and create financial instability.Barr raised concerns about the growing use of AI agents in retail banking, noting that banks could struggle to establish whether an AI system attempting to access or operate customer accounts has received proper authorisation. Even legitimate AI agents acting on behalf of customers could accelerate bank runs by moving money at unprecedented speeds, potentially overwhelming traditional safeguards, the report stated.Also Read |Chinese yuan steadies near two-week peak ahead of Xi-Trump meetingCybersecurity presents another significant challenge, with AI-enabled attackers and rogue AI agents potentially exploiting vulnerabilities across the financial system, Barr said.He also cautioned that AI developers face challenges in ensuring their models are properly controlled, legally precise, explainable and reproducible. The technology could reinforce existing biases in consumer lending and create risks of collusion, market manipulation and trading strategies capable of triggering significant volatility or systemic instability.Barr's comments, prepared for delivery in Milan, Italy, came ahead of a conference at the San Francisco Federal Reserve, where Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was scheduled to bring together AI developers, business leaders and academics to discuss the technology's implications for productivity, employment and the broader economy.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: South Korean shares close at over 9-month low on Nvidia caution
item.description: South Korean shares experienced a significant decline of more than 2% amid concerns affecting chipmakers. The benchmark KOSPI closed at its lowest level since February due to persistent selling pressure. Foreign investors were noted as net sellers of shares worth approximately 1.4 trillion won. The Korean won weakened slightly against the dollar during this trading period. Additionally, South Korea's benchmark bond yields fell as market activities shifted.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:South Korean shares fell more than 2% on Tuesday to a nine-month closing low, as chipmakers dropped on US curbs against China and caution ahead of Nvidia's earnings.The benchmark KOSPI closed 132.02 points, or 2.59% lower, at 4,968.48, its lowest since February 2, in a fourth consecutive session of losses.A broad selloff dragged US stocks lower on Monday as fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO soured enthusiasm for AI stocks.The Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening controls as President Donald Trump headed to China for talks with President Xi Jinping. There was selling pressure amid high uncertainty ahead of Nvidia's earnings, said Seo Sang-young, an analyst at Mirae Asset Securities.Chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 3.3%, while peer SK Hynix lost 1.96%.Index heavyweights such as battery maker LG Energy Solution slid 4.08%, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were down 2.45% and 3.05%, respectively.Steelmaker POSCO Holdings shed 2.61%, while drugmaker Samsung Biologics fell 0.63%.Of the total 912 traded issues, 185 shares advanced, while 709 declined.Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion).The won was quoted at 1,338.2 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, 0.13% lower than its previous close at 1,336.5.In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds added 0.04 of a point to 103.52.The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield fell by 1.2 basis points to 3.727%, while the benchmark 10-year yield fell by 0.8 basis points to 3.974%.
